steps.what: Review clients' aptitudes, education levels, physical abilities and career goals
Develop rehabilitation plans that fit the client's circumstances and agreed goals

tasks.design: Keep plan development with the counsellor and client, supported by the {OTHER} case-management system. Do not infer goals or prescribe a rehabilitation route from a generated summary.
tasks.previous_blocker: A workable plan depends on individual circumstances and agreement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case records support the unchanged planning process.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing aspirations, abilities, available services and changing circumstances.
tasks.human_edge: Develop a realistic plan with the client rather than select it for them.
tasks.altitude: Planning responsibilities and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Rehabilitation plan development is retained as professional and client judgement; note-drafting capability does not establish plan-making capability.

assumptions: Boundary is interpretation and plan development after the initial goals discussion; the separate discussion task is not added again for the same encounter.
Counsellor reviews existing assessments and client-stated goals in s1; missing information is discussed rather than assumed to be structured.
The case-management system stores the agreed plan; no software change or incremental upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Local service options and planning responsibilities
research_questions: Which client circumstances require specialist input before a plan is agreed?

approvals.approved_version: Exact plan, client-stated goals and supporting assessment version; changed goals or circumstances require renewed review

steps.what: Verify client information, services provided and facts from client contacts
Prepare records, case files and client-contact narratives

loop.purpose: Draft a structured note from verified contact facts
loop.input: Counsellor-confirmed facts, source references and note structure
loop.output: Draft case note with explicit source attribution and missing information
loop.check: Counsellor compares meaning, client voice, chronology, eligibility facts and every risk statement against source notes; unsupported risk statements are removed
loop.stop: One revision; unclear attribution, missing facts or changed risk meaning return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Fields handle identifiers but cannot express the varied meaning of contact narratives

steps.what: Check the completed record and file the approved version

tasks.design: Use native fields in the {OTHER} case-management system before adding a bounded drafting loop for contact narratives. The counsellor verifies source facts and approves the exact record; no eligibility or risk decision is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact facts are repeatedly rewritten into formal case notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Care documentation tools can convert dictated notes into structured reports.
tasks.still_hard: Nuance, attribution and risk statements can be altered by a fluent draft.
tasks.human_edge: Preserve the client's meaning and the distinction between observation and inference.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft note writing only if full review leaves a net gain.

reach.task: Maintain complete and correctly routed case records

evidence.claim: Attendi turns dictated notes into structured reports or letters in care records.
The Hengelo summary pilot retained consultants' own notes and saved little time, particularly for complex cases.
The proposed rehabilitation case-record saving is a scenario, not a measured local result.

assumptions: Boundary is case documentation after client work, excluding the counselling encounter, plan decision and eligibility assessment.

Counsellor produces client id, contact date, verified personal details, services, relevant statements and source references in s1's full35 hours. Existing providers retain their own service records; no new structured capture is transferred.
Use existing notes or authorised post-contact dictation; dictation and source-pack preparation are included in s1. No free recording transcript is assumed. Missing facts are verified manually.
Meaning correction20 hours and final filing checks25 hours remain counted. Test native note templates first and use only an approved environment.
The draft cannot establish eligibility, infer risk or replace an existing professional decision.
research_questions: Do complete-note trials preserve meaning and risk statements after all preparation and correction time is included?

incremental.description: Maintain note structure and review recurring draft errors
Maintain approved access and record integration

approvals.approved_version: Exact client record, source references, note content and access destination; changes require renewed counsellor review

steps.what: Locate barriers such as inaccessible work sites, inflexible schedules or transportation problems
Work with clients to develop strategies for overcoming the identified barriers

tasks.design: Keep barrier identification and strategy development with the counsellor and client. Existing service information in {DOCS} can inform choices, with no automated employability score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Barriers depend on the client's real work and travel circumstances.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software is necessary for joint problem solving.
tasks.still_hard: An available adjustment may not be practical or acceptable to the client.
tasks.human_edge: Understand lived constraints and develop workable choices together.

evidence.claim: Barrier identification and joint strategy development remain fully counted personal work.

assumptions: Boundary is barrier-specific counselling, excluding general goals discussion and later plan documentation; overlapping encounters are allocated once.
Client and counsellor establish actual constraints during s1, with direct clarification when information is missing. No structured accessibility flag or travel profile is assumed.
No new system or incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Local transport, employer and accessibility options
research_questions: Which identified barrier prevents the client using an otherwise suitable opportunity?
